The project API did not check that the caller owns, or has been granted access to, the project being accessed. Any authenticated user with an approved account (the REGULAR or ADMIN role; new accounts need administrator approval by default) could view, modify or delete other users' projects, change which workflows those projects contain, and see the e-mail addresses of a project's owner and collaborators. The project feature is hidden in the web UI by default, but the API was reachable regardless of that setting. This issue affects Apache Texera: from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue by removing the deprecated project feature and its data. If you cannot upgrade immediately, configure the reverse proxy in front of Texera to reject every request whose path starts with /api/project, /api/public/project or /api/access/project, and every request whose path contains ';', which the Texera server ignores when routing. Respond with 403 or 404, not 401: from 1.2.0-incubating the web UI treats a 401 as an expired session, and the workflow pages request the project list when they load. Unless an administrator has enabled the project feature, this does not affect other functionality; those project-list requests are simply rejected. Make sure the Texera server is reachable only through that proxy. Blocking and upgrading do not undo access obtained earlier. Before upgrading, review the project, project_user_access and workflow_of_project tables, which remain empty unless someone has used the feature, and remove rows you do not expect; the upgrade deletes these tables. Do not copy project grants into workflow_user_access without checking each one.

CVE-2026-96354.description: Missing Authorization vulnerability in the public project REST API of Apache Texera (incubating). The public project API did not check that a project had been made public before granting the caller read access to it. Any authenticated user with an approved account (the REGULAR or ADMIN role; new accounts need administrator approval by default) could give themselves lasting read access to other users' private projects and to the private workflows in them, including their version and execution history. Only deployments in which users have created projects are affected; the project feature is hidden in the web UI by default. This issue affects Apache Texera: from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue by removing the deprecated project feature and its data. If you cannot upgrade immediately, configure the reverse proxy in front of Texera to reject every request whose path starts with /api/project, /api/public/project or /api/access/project, and every request whose path contains ';', which the Texera server ignores when routing. Respond with 403 or 404, not 401: from 1.2.0-incubating the web UI treats a 401 as an expired session, and the workflow pages request the project list when they load. Unless an administrator has enabled the project feature, this does not affect other functionality; those project-list requests are simply rejected. Make sure the Texera server is reachable only through that proxy. Blocking and upgrading do not undo access obtained earlier. Before upgrading, review the project_user_access table, which remains empty unless someone has used the feature: treat any READ grant on a project that is not listed in public_project, and that the project's owner did not give, as suspect. The upgrade deletes this table. Removing a grant does not remove copies the user may already have made of the workflows.

CVE-2026-97893.description: A Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability exists in the ARQ SPARQL Query Optimiser in Apache Jena ARQ prior to version 6.3.0 that allows a SPARQL query to use that cause excessive memory usage. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.3.0, which fixes this issue. Users who are unable to upgrade immediately, especially those who operate a public facing SPARQL service/application backed by Apache Jena are recommended to configure the ARQ symbol arq:optPathFlatten=false in their SPARQL execution context which disables the problematic optimisation.

CVE-2026-103333.description: Improper input validation in some SPARQL functions available in Apache Jena ARQ allows users to submit SPARQL queries that cause excessive CPU and/or memory usage. This may be the result of intentionally malicious inputs in the query itself, or an expression applied over data that has been insufficiently validated/sanitised Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.3.0, which fixes this issue.

CVE-2026-103756.description: Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknolojileri Grubu Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows XSS Through HTTP Headers. This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.3 before v14.08.5.

CVE-2026-104813.description: Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory ('path traversal') vulnerability in Apache BuildStream allows malicious or compromised artifact or execution servers to write files on the host, with the privileges of the user running BuildStream, as part of `bst artifact checkout`. The impact of this issue is mitigated by: * BuildStream projects should only use trusted servers for remote cache and remote execution as otherwise the build output can also not be trusted This issue affects Apache BuildStream: through 2.8.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.8.2, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-10765.description: RTU500 contains a denial-of-service vulnerability in its IEC 61850 MMS server implementation. A malicious user with access to the IEC 61850 interface can trigger improper handling of asynchronous control operations involving special response and timing criteria. This may result in access to invalid memory structures, leading to a software exception, loss of IEC 61850 communications, or device reboot.

CVE-2026-111600.description: UNIX symbolic link (symlink) following vulnerability in Apache BuildStream allows source plugins to inadvertently read or write files on the host, with the privileges of the user running BuildStream, via symlinks from malicious or compromised source archives or respositories, as part of source fetching. The impact of this issue is mitigated by: * BuildStream projects should only use trusted sources in their elements as otherwise the build output can also not be trusted * None of the source plugins in the buildstream, buildstream-plugins or buildstream-plugins-community repositories use the vulnerable `open_file` method This issue affects Apache BuildStream: through 2.8.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.8.2, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-117593.description: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknoloji Grubu Tic. Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows Password Recovery Exploitation. This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.3 before v14.08.5.

CVE-2026-119543.description: Authorization bypass through User-Controlled key vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknoloji Grubu Tic. Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs. This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.3 before v14.08.5.

CVE-2026-119582.description: Improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command ('SQL injection') vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknoloji Grubu Tic. Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows SQL Injection. This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.3 before v14.08.5.

CVE-2026-121375.description: Reflected cross-site scripting in the versioned REST API documentation page in Checkmk versions 2.5.0 before 2.5.0p21 allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of a user who opens a crafted link, in the context of that user's Checkmk session. The API version segment of the documentation URL is inserted into the page without escaping, and the page is reachable without authentication.

CVE-2026-125735.description: SQL injection in the CabinPaq manual code entry module, versions v.1.2.94 and v.1.2.136. The application constructs SQL queries from terminal input without properly sanitising it. With physical access to the terminal, an attacker could bypass code validation and open compartments without authorisation.

CVE-2026-126605.description: Authentication bypass in the Face ID app lock in Proton Pass for iOS before v. 1.21.1 allows an attacker with physical access to an already unlocked device to open vault items behind the lock screen via VoiceOver, leading to the disclosure and modification of stored credentials.

CVE-2026-128420.description: A heap buffer overflow issue exists in the rms_mqtt daemon on Teltonika Networks devices. An authenticated attacker with access to the affected service could trigger a heap-based buffer overflow, resulting in a denial of service. This issue affects RUT: from 7.0 through 7.18.0; RUTX: from 7.0 through 7.18.0; RUTM: from 7.0 through 7.18.0; RUTC: from 7.0 through 7.18.0; ATRM: from 7.16.1 through 7.18.0; TRB: from 7.0 through 7.18.0; OTD: from 7.11.1 through 7.18.0; TAP: from 7.4.3 through 7.18.0; DAP: from 7.12 through 7.18.0; SWM: from 1.6.3 through 1.7.1; TSW: from 1.1 through 1.7.1.

CVE-2026-134858.description: In Apache Pinot 0.7.1 through 1.5.1, a caller who can submit URI ingestion jobs can select local files readable by the controller process. If the file can be ingested using the destination table’s schema and input format, users with query access to that table can read its contents. Upgrade to Apache Pinot 1.6.0 and keep controller.ingestFromURI.allowLocalFileSystem at its default value of false on every controller. Until you can upgrade, block the URI ingestion endpoint if it is unused or restrict it to trusted operators.

CVE-2026-135660.description: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS) vulnerability in Apache Allura's ticket tracking tool. This issue affects Apache Allura: before 1.23.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.23.0, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-135747.description: Apache IoTDB MCP Server logs the IoTDB connection password in plaintext during startup, allowing anyone with access to the logs to obtain the credential. This issue affects Apache IoTDB MCP Server: through 0.2.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.3.0, which fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-13137.description: A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in multiple parsers of RTU500 components of User management, REST resolver and SPA-Bus. Attacker controlled input can influence the length of data copied into fixed-size stack buffers without proper bounds checking, which may result in memory corruption leading to denial of service condition.

CVE-2026-59697.description: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in ex_aws (instance metadata token provider). This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/instance_meta_token_provider.ex and program routines ExAws.InstanceMetaTokenProvider.request_token/1 and ExAws.InstanceMetaTokenProvider.get/1. ex_aws requests its IMDSv2 session token from the link-local metadata endpoint (http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token) with HTTP redirect following enabled. Because the token request follows 3xx redirects and does not restrict the redirect target to the link-local range, an attacker who can influence the response to the metadata request (for example an on-segment neighbor spoofing the link-local address) can answer with a redirect to an arbitrary host. The library follows the redirect and accepts the arbitrary host's response body as the IMDSv2 session token, caching it and sending it as the x-aws-ec2-metadata-token header on every subsequent metadata and credential request. This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.3.0 before 2.8.0.

CVE-2026-59698.description: Relative path traversal in ex_aws allows an attacker who controls an S3 object key to escape the intended bucket or key prefix. When ex_aws builds a path-style S3 request, ExAws.Operation.S3.add_bucket_to_path/2 in lib/ex_aws/operation/s3.ex joins the bucket name and the object key into a single path string and then normalizes it, collapsing . and .. segments the way a filesystem path would. Because the bucket is the first segment of the combined string, a leading ../ in the object key pops the bucket off the path. With bucket mybucket and a key of ../victim/secret.txt, the combined /mybucket/../victim/secret.txt normalizes to /victim/secret.txt, so the request (signed with the application's own credentials) is sent to bucket victim. The same mechanism collapses ../ within a key, defeating any isolation an application enforces by prepending a trusted prefix. Only the default path-style configuration is affected; requests built with virtual_host: true do not run this normalization. Because S3 treats object keys as opaque and does not resolve .. itself, the client-side normalization introduces a traversal that would not otherwise exist. Any application that derives an S3 object key from untrusted input and relies on the bucket, or a key prefix, as a tenant or trust boundary is exposed to cross-bucket or cross-prefix read and write, depending on the operation and the credentials' permissions. This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.1.7 before 2.8.0.

CVE-2026-62269.description: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output vulnerability in ex_aws (S3 request URL construction). This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/request/url.ex and program routines ExAws.Request.Url.build/2, ExAws.Request.Url.sanitize/2 and ExAws.Request.Url.get_path/2. ex_aws does not percent-encode reserved characters in S3 object keys when it assembles the request URL. A literal ? in an object key survives unencoded: build/2 inserts the operation path verbatim and URI.to_string/1 emits it without encoding, and sanitize/2 then splits the flattened URL on the first ?, treating everything after it as the query string. Because the split runs before uri_encode is applied to the path, the ? is never neutralized, and the recovered query is re-inserted without any encoding. An attacker who controls part of an object key (for example a download or upload keyed by a user-supplied filename) can therefore truncate the key past application-appended suffixes, causing the request to address a different object than the application intended, and can inject live S3 sub-resource operations (such as ?acl, ?tagging or ?versions) into the request. The manipulated URL is signed and transmitted normally, so the tampering is authorized like any legitimate request. This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.1.2 before 2.8.0.

CVE-2026-84785.description: Issue summary: A QUIC peer that sends many small out-of-order STREAM fragments while withholding the first byte of the stream may cause OpenSSL to buffer a large number of reassembly nodes occupying much larger memory than the actual data sent. Impact summary: A remote peer can pin large amounts of memory on a server that accepts incoming QUIC streams, potentially exhausting memory and causing Denial of Service. CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling Description: QUIC receive flow control limits the highest byte offset a peer may reach on a stream. It does not limit how many out-of-order fragments the receiver buffers. OpenSSL allocates a reassembly node for each non-adjacent STREAM fragment and never caps the count. A peer that opens a stream and sends many one-byte fragments at increasing offsets, while withholding the first byte, makes the receiver retain one node per fragment without delivering any data. Only applications that accept incoming streams are exposed. With the default policy, which rejects peer-initiated streams, the stream is torn down before state accumulates. Because the read side never advances past the missing prefix, the flow control window never slides and the nodes stay pinned for the life of the connection. The per-stream window bounds the highest offset, so the memory one stream can pin is finite, but it can reach tens of megabytes and, across many streams and connections, drive memory pressure and Denial of Service. The severity is limited because the exhaustion is bounded by flow control and requires a non-default configuration. FIPS impact: no The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

CVE-2026-94365.description: Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknolojileri Grubu Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows XSS Through HTTP Headers. This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.1 before v14.08.5.

CVE-2026-96438.description: Unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknolojileri Grubu Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows Using Malicious Files. This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.1 before v14.08.5.

CVE-2026-97198.description: Authorization bypass through User-Controlled key vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknolojileri Grubu Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows Privilege Abuse. This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.1 before v14.08.5.

CVE-2026-120720.description: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws allows an attacker who controls an S3 bucket name to send the application's signed S3 requests to a host of their choice. With virtual_host: true, ExAws.Operation.S3.add_bucket_to_path/2 in lib/ex_aws/operation/s3.ex builds the request hostname from the bucket name and the configured host without checking the bucket name. A bucket such as attacker.example/x? turns the request URL into https://attacker.example/x?.s3.amazonaws.com/key, so the request is signed for and sent to attacker.example. The attacker receives upload bodies, the access key id and request signature, and any STS session token, and controls the response the application parses. With bucket_as_host: true the bucket is the whole hostname, so any valid hostname redirects the request. This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.1.7 before 2.8.0.

CVE-2026-124268.description: Missing Authorization vulnerability in Arraytics WP Event Solution wp-event-solution allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects WP Event Solution: from n/a through 4.1.30.

CVE-2026-124273.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Arraytics WP Event Solution wp-event-solution allows Stored XSS.This issue affects WP Event Solution: from n/a through 4.1.30.

CVE-2026-124754.description: RTU500 has a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability through the NCMD metric name present in the Sparkplug payload of the MQTT message received, resulting in Denial of Service.

CVE-2026-125441.description: Missing Authorization vulnerability in Arraytics WP Event Solution wp-event-solution allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects WP Event Solution: from n/a through 4.1.30.

CVE-2026-127181.description: SUSE Neuvector before 5.5, 5.5.0 before 5.5.6 and 5.6.0 before 5.6.5 handling of ephemeral containers was not setting some checking callbacks, allowing these to bypass permission checks.

CVE-2026-133763.description: The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. For an object, the is true test evaluates to the object itself, and that result wasn't checked. A sandboxed template could therefore print an object through a denied toString() method: {{ obj is true }} The same applies when the result is concatenated or passed to a filter. No tag needs to be allowed. A test in a boolean context, like {% if obj is true %}, isn't affected, since it doesn't convert the object to a string. The sandbox now checks the result of tests like the result of filters and functions.

CVE-2026-133764.description: The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. It didn't check the input of tests. The PHP callable of a test may convert this input to a string, for example when its parameter is typed as string. PHP then calls toString() on an object without the sandbox checking it first: {{ obj is upperish }} Applications are affected when they register such a test and allow it in the sandbox. No built-in test is affected. The sandbox now checks the input of tests like the input of filters. The built-in tests that never convert their input to a string still skip the check.

CVE-2026-133765.description: The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. Since Twig 3.23.0, assignments like x = obj, and the destructuring forms [a] = list and {a} = obj, evaluate to the value that they assign. The sandbox didn't check that value, so a sandboxed template could call a denied toString() method: {{ (x = obj) }} {{ ({secret: s} = obj)|join }} No tag needs to be allowed. The sandbox now checks the result of assignments like the result of filters and functions. {% do x = obj %} and {% if (x = obj) %} still work, since they don't convert the value to a string.

CVE-2026-133766.description: Since Twig 3.28.0, the sandbox skips the toString() check of an argument whose PHP parameter can't hold a string, like an int. A spread argument was mapped to a single parameter, although it fills every parameter from its position on. A sandboxed template could therefore call a denied toString() method: {{ tag(...[1, obj]) }} Here, the first parameter of tag() is an int, and a later one accepts strings. Applications are affected when they allow such a function, filter or test in the sandbox. No built-in callable is affected. A spread argument is now checked unless every parameter that it can fill has a safe type.

CVE-2026-133767.description: When the parent of an embed tag was an expression other than a string or a variable, the sandbox didn't see that expression. The functions, filters and tests of the expression weren't checked against the policy, and neither were its conversions to strings. A sandboxed template allowed to use embed could therefore call any function, filter or test, and any __toString() method: {% embed 'leak_' ~ app_secret() %}{% endembed %} Method calls and property reads were not affected, since they're checked at runtime. The sandbox now checks the parent expression of embed like any other expression of the template.

CVE-2026-133768.description: The join filter converted a value that isn't iterable with (array) $value. For an object, that gives every property, including the private and protected ones. A sandboxed template allowed to use join could therefore print properties that the policy denies, and that templates can't read otherwise: {{ user|join(',') }} A value that isn't iterable is now joined as a single item. A Stringable object prints its checked string, and other objects throw, as with the first and last filters.

CVE-2026-133769.description: Cva::apply() converted the values of variants, default variants and compound variants with (array). These values come from the arguments of html_cva(). A sandboxed template could therefore pass any object of its context, and print the private and protected properties of that object: {{ html_cva('base', {c: {p: user}}).apply({c: 'p'}) }} Variant maps that are ArrayAccess objects were also read with a key that the template chooses, without the property check of the sandbox. The template then printed the offsets that the object returned. Applications are affected when the sandbox allows the html_cva function and the apply method of Twig\Extra\Html\Cva. A value that isn't an array is now treated as a single item, so objects are dropped and never match a variant. Variant maps are also only used when they're arrays.

CVE-2026-133770.description: The sandbox allows every method of Twig\Markup objects, including their public constructor. A sandboxed template can therefore call __construct() on any Markup object that it reaches, and replace its content: {% do banner.__construct('<script>alert(1)</script>', 'UTF-8') %} A template gains nothing by rewriting its own output. The impact is on the Markup objects that come from the application and are also rendered elsewhere, like a global in a long-running worker. Their new content then ends up in trusted pages that aren't sandboxed. The sandbox no longer allows calling the constructor of Markup objects.

CVE-2026-133771.description: The escaper considered x.attr, x['key'] and x.method() safe whenever {% import ... as x %} appeared anywhere in the template. Macro calls haven't needed this rule since Twig 3.0. It only matched ordinary variables that have the name of an alias imported in another block or macro, and printed them without escaping: {% block header %}{% import _self as item %}{{ item.hello() }}{% endblock %} {% block content %}{% for item in items %}{{ item.body }}{% endfor %}{% endblock %} Here, item.body is printed raw. This leads to XSS when the value comes from an attacker. The same happens with an import in a macro and an argument of the same name in another macro. It also happens with a template-level import placed after the block that uses the name. The rule is removed. Macro calls through an alias are still considered safe.

CVE-2026-133772.description: The guard tag compiles only one of its branches, depending on whether a callable exists. The other branch was still parsed, though. The extends, use, macro and block tags in it registered their effects on the template. The sandbox doesn't see these tags, since that branch isn't compiled. A sandboxed template allowed to use guard could therefore extend a template, import blocks and define macros, while the policy doesn't allow these tags: {% guard filter upper %}{% else %}{% extends "parent.html" %}{% endguard %} The templates reached this way come from the loader of the sandbox, and they are sandboxed too. What the branch that isn't selected registers on the parser is now discarded.

CVE-2026-133773.description: The html_to_markdown filter of twig/markdown-extra keeps an HtmlConverter for each distinct mapping of options it receives. They're kept in a static array, with no size limit and no eviction. The options are an argument of the filter. A template that passes options taken from the input, or a sandboxed template, can therefore make this cache grow without limit. The cache outlives the environment, so it fills the memory of long-running workers. The cache now keeps at most 100 converters, like the formatter caches of IntlExtension.

CVE-2026-62270.description: Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input in ExAws.Dynamo.Encoder.encode/2 in ex_aws_dynamo allows an attacker who controls map data passed into a DynamoDB call to choose the raw stored DynamoDB AttributeValue. The encode/2 function in lib/ex_aws/dynamo/encoder.ex has one clause per DynamoDB type descriptor ("S", "N", "B", "BOOL", "M", "L", "NS", "SS", "BS", "NULL") that treats any map merely containing such a key as already encoded and returns it verbatim, bypassing the ExAws.Dynamo.Encodable protocol. The match is on the presence of the key alone, so no check is made that the value is well formed for the claimed type, and extra keys and arbitrary nested content survive untouched. An application that threads user-influenced map data (a decoded JSON body, a nested attribute, or an expression_attribute_values entry) into a Dynamo write or query therefore lets the user, rather than the application, decide the stored attribute's declared type, its bytes, and its structure. This type confusion breaks round-trip integrity and enables silent persistent data corruption, injection of attributes and raw binaries the schema never sanctioned, subversion of application authorization checks that trust the decoded type of a value, and a decoder crash on read-back that denies reads of the affected item to other users of the same table. This issue affects ex_aws_dynamo: from 2.0.0 before 4.3.0.

CVE-2026-62271.description: Use of RSA Algorithm without OAEP vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_kms (ExAws.KMS module) causes callers who import external key material to wrap their secret KMS key material with the deprecated PKCS#1 v1.5 padding scheme by default. This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/ex_aws/kms.ex and program routine ExAws.KMS.get_parameters_for_import/3. ExAws.KMS.get_parameters_for_import/3 defaults its wrapping_algorithm argument to "RSAES_PKCS1_V1_5". AWS KMS returns this value as the WrappingAlgorithm for the import operation, and it dictates the RSA padding scheme the caller uses to wrap (RSA-encrypt) their secret key material before calling ImportKeyMaterial. AWS KMS also supports the stronger RSAES_OAEP_SHA_1 and RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256 schemes. By defaulting to RSAES_PKCS1_V1_5, the library steers callers who do not explicitly override the argument toward the weakest of the three. PKCS#1 v1.5 encryption padding is susceptible to Bleichenbacher adaptive chosen-ciphertext (padding oracle) attacks, which can recover the wrapped plaintext without the private key given an oracle that reveals whether a decrypted value was validly padded. Because the unwrap happens inside AWS KMS, which does not expose a padding oracle, the practical exploitability is low and this is a defense-in-depth weakness. Callers can avoid the weak default by explicitly passing "RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256" (or "RSAES_OAEP_SHA_1") as the wrapping algorithm. This issue affects ex_aws_kms: from 2.1.0 before 2.7.0.

CVE-2026-120299.description: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in ash-project ash allows an attacker to bypass the input validation of the field types of a :keyword attribute or argument. Ash.Type.Keyword.cast_input/2 in lib/ash/type/keyword.ex converts a map input to a keyword list in try_map_to_keyword/2, which casts each declared field with Ash.Type.cast_stored/3. That function is meant for trusted values read back from the data layer, so client input skips the cast_input/2 of each field type. apply_constraints/2 casts the result again with cast_input/2, but most types accept a value of their own type unchanged. An embedded resource field is built without its create action, so its validations and changes do not run and its non-public attributes can be set. A :function field accepts a capture string such as &Mod.fun/1, and a :term field decodes Erlang external term format. This issue affects ash: from 3.24.0 before 3.38.1.

CVE-2026-129514.description: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in the application/vnd.hex+erlang request body parser in hexpm hexpm allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute operating system commands via a crafted Erlang external term format request body. This vulnerability was actively exploited against the hex.pm service on 2026-11-23. HexpmWeb.ErlangFormat.decode/1 in lib/hexpm_web/erlang_format.ex decodes the body with Plug.Crypto.non_executable_binary_to_term/2, which accepts maps that have a __struct__ key. HexpmWeb.PlugParser.parse/5 returns the decoded term as the request params. The parser runs in the endpoint before routing and authentication, so a POST to any route reaches it. Elixir dispatches protocols on the __struct__ key, so the client selects which Inspect and Enumerable implementations run when error reporting inspects the params. A chain through Ecto.Query.DynamicExpr and DBConnection.Stream reaches an apply/3 call on a {module, function, args} tuple taken from the request body. This issue affects hex.pm: from 2016-02-23 before 2026-11-23; hexpm/hexpm: from ab1bbcef7cc8395d1056d3b1aa6a174353492d59 before 379b0a29bcc95164249f38ad7d772a37a8ff9533.

CVE-2026-130822.description: In Valkey before 7.2.16, 8.0.x before 8.0.13, 8.1.x before 8.1.12, 9.0.x before 9.0.8, 9.1.x before 9.1.4 and 9.2.0 release candidates, when client eviction is enabled (maxmemory-clients is not 0), an authenticated user who can write to a key that other clients are blocked on (for example with BLPOP, BLMPOP, BZPOPMIN or XREAD BLOCK) can trigger a use-after-free. While the clients blocked on that key are served, evictClients() can select and free the client whose command made the key ready, although that command is still executing, and the server then keeps using the freed client. The blocked clients do not have to belong to the attacker. The result is a reliable crash of the server process. Servers with the default maxmemory-clients 0 are not affected.

CVE-2026-136152.description: Prevent Direct Access – Protect WordPress Files plugin before 2.8.9.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain protected file names and paths by requesting the dynamically generated robots.txt file, which appends Disallow rules containing attachment page URLs and direct _pda/ directory file paths for all protected media. Attackers can send an unauthenticated HTTP request to robots.txt to enumerate original file names, upload directory structures, and attachment slugs, undermining the plugin's file protection and potentially enabling direct file access if server-level restrictions are misconfigured or absent.

7631e3d74c1dc8542d910191.title_ko: 삼성SDS, AX·AI 인프라 사업 확대 위해 임원 진용 재편
7631e3d74c1dc8542d910191.summary_ko: 삼성SDS가 2027년 정기 임원 인사에서 부사장 4명과 상무 6명 등 총 10명을 승진시켰다. 전체 승진 규모는 지난해와 같지만 부사장 승진자는 두 배로 늘었으며, 회사는 AX서비스와 AI인프라 등 미래 성장동력 사업 확대와 기술 경쟁력 강화를 추진할 계획이라고 밝혔다.
7631e3d74c1dc8542d910191.background_ko: 삼성SDS는 기업 AX·클라우드 등에서 성과를 낸 리더를 발탁해 현장 중심 리더십을 강화하고 미래 성장동력 사업을 확대하려는 취지라고 설명했다.

6760cb94e5ec0616aa9f0b07.title_ko: 젠슨 황 복귀 소식에 국내 AI 인프라 관련주 반등 보도
6760cb94e5ec0616aa9f0b07.summary_ko: 기사는 젠슨 황의 엔비디아 CEO 복귀 소식 이후 엘리스그룹·래블업·씨이랩 주가가 각각 7.58%, 4.28%, 7.09% 상승했다고 전했다. 증권가는 AI 생태계의 연속성에 대한 불안 완화를 반등 배경으로 보면서도, 엔비디아 관련 조사·규제와 AI 인프라 수요의 실적 전환 여부는 불확실성으로 지적했다고 소개했다.
6760cb94e5ec0616aa9f0b07.background_ko: 기사는 황 CEO 복귀로 AI 생태계의 연속성에 대한 불안이 완화됐다는 증권가 분석을 관련주 반등의 배경으로 제시했다.

60fddaa0bf0d9799399ac429.title_ko: AWS, AI 에이전트 도구 작업 증가에 자체 CPU·클라우드 인프라 강화
60fddaa0bf0d9799399ac429.summary_ko: AWS는 AI 에이전트의 API 호출·코드 실행 같은 도구 작업을 지원하기 위해 자체 CPU 그래비톤 중심의 인프라를 강화한다고 밝혔다. 에이전트 작업의 80%를 CPU가 처리한다는 설명과 함께 AWS AI 팩토리와 격리 실행 환경을 소개하고, 기업 데이터를 지식 그래프로 연결하는 AWS 컨텍스트 출시 계획도 공개했다.
60fddaa0bf0d9799399ac429.background_ko: AWS는 에이전트가 모델 추론보다 API 호출·코드 실행 등 CPU 기반 도구 작업에 많은 연산자원을 사용한다고 설명했다.

curation.reason_ko: AWS가 에이전트의 도구 실행을 지원할 자체 CPU·격리 환경과 데이터 연결 전략을 소개했다.

2c714469d1e303f3f6b49787.title_ko: KrrK 팀원, 대학생 개인정보 판매 주장…실제 침해·거래 확인은 제한적
2c714469d1e303f3f6b49787.summary_ko: KrrK 팀원이라고 밝힌 인물이 국내 대학의 학생 개인정보를 판매했다며 추가 공격 대상 사이트 목록을 제시했다. 그러나 거래 기록이나 유출 규모 등 입증 자료는 공개하지 않아 실제 침해·판매 여부는 확인되지 않았다. 기사는 특정 하위 사이트가 지목됐다는 사실을 대학 전체의 피해로 확대 해석해서는 안 된다고 강조했다.

0419a40675846c3d6aaab08f.title_ko: 멤텐서·엔비디아, 대화 기억을 내부에 저장하는 멤T-1.0 프로 공개
0419a40675846c3d6aaab08f.summary_ko: 멤텐서가 엔비디아와 협력해 과거 대화를 내부 기억 상태로 저장·활용하는 AI 모델 멤T-1.0 프로를 공개하고 가중치와 사용 코드를 배포했다. 연구진 자체 평가에서는 매개변수 기반 기억 방식 중 높은 성능을 보였지만, 원문을 저장·검색하는 주요 시스템보다 종합 점수가 낮았고 긴 기록의 세부 근거 검색에는 한계가 있었다.
0419a40675846c3d6aaab08f.background_ko: 과거 대화 원문을 매번 프롬프트에 다시 넣는 부담을 줄이고 여러 세션에 걸쳐 이전 정보를 활용하도록 개발됐다.

curation.reason_ko: 대화 정보를 내부 기억에 저장하는 모델의 가중치·코드와 검색 방식 대비 한계가 함께 공개됐다.

650e1d85acdaad08713cbc7e.title_ko: 말레이시아, 제재 기업 데이터센터 이용 제한 권고…싱가포르도 칩 우회 조사
650e1d85acdaad08713cbc7e.summary_ko: 말레이시아는 미국 수출통제 명단에 새로 오른 기업 7곳에 데이터센터 입주·임대·서비스를 제공하지 않도록 권고할 예정이다. 기존 계약의 즉각 해지를 명령한 것은 아니다. 싱가포르는 첨단 반도체 우회 공급을 막기 위한 미국 조사에 협력하고, 메가스피드 등 현지 기업의 법 위반 여부도 조사하고 있다고 밝혔다.

7c4ae7c97e7be641397e2199.background_ko: 서울형 R&D는 기업의 기술 개발과 사업화를 돕기 위해 서울시와 서울경제진흥원이 추진하는 지원사업이다.

116ba79f2c78eb746c8d07d3.title_original: Microsoft Azure flaw exploited to steal customers' API credentials
116ba79f2c78eb746c8d07d3.excerpt: Microsoft is warning customers that a security vulnerability in Azure API Management (APIM) Classic tiers was exploited to steal stored API credentials, with Norwegian authorities linking the flaw to cyberattacks against energy companies. [...]
116ba79f2c78eb746c8d07d3.title_ko: Azure API Management 취약점 악용으로 고객 API 자격 증명 탈취
116ba79f2c78eb746c8d07d3.summary_ko: Microsoft는 Azure API Management Classic 일부 요금제의 취약점이 저장된 API 자격 증명을 탈취하는 데 악용됐다고 경고했다. 11월 19일 무단 접근 경로를 차단했지만, 이미 노출된 고객 자격 증명은 자동 무효화되지 않아 교체가 필요하다고 밝혔다. APIM v2와 Classic의 Consumption 요금제는 영향이 없다고 설명했다.
116ba79f2c78eb746c8d07d3.background_ko: Microsoft에 따르면 보안 권장 설정을 따르지 않은 APIM Classic 인스턴스에서 취약점을 통해 관리 기능과 저장된 비밀정보에 무단 접근할 수 있었다.

curation.reason_ko: 저장된 API 자격증명 탈취가 확인돼 영향 고객의 자격증명 교체가 필요하다.

a7177446c2699b431b8ddb89.title_original: 젠슨 황, 사임 11일 만에 엔비디아 CEO 복귀…트럼프 직접 개입

a7177446c2699b431b8ddb89.title_ko: 젠슨 황, 사임 11일 만에 엔비디아 CEO 복귀 보도
a7177446c2699b431b8ddb89.summary_ko: 기사에 따르면 엔비디아 이사회는 사임 11일 만에 젠슨 황의 CEO·사장·이사직 복귀를 만장일치로 승인했다. 트럼프 대통령의 개입과 국가안보 관련 정부 의견이 결정에 영향을 줬으며, 외국 정보기관 접근 의혹 조사와 당국 조사·주주 소송은 계속되고 있다고 전했다.
a7177446c2699b431b8ddb89.background_ko: 기사에 따르면 이사회는 황과의 면담과 미국 정부 고위 당국자 의견 청취를 거쳐, 신뢰 회복과 국가안보 위험이 없다는 판단을 복귀 승인 근거로 제시했다.

curation.reason_ko: 정부 개입 이후 CEO 복귀가 승인됐다는 보도로 AI 반도체 핵심 기업의 지배구조 변화다.

ffd5ce4b071046c10a21802f.title_original: OpenRouter drops AI providers over leaked prompts and secrets
ffd5ce4b071046c10a21802f.excerpt: OpenRouter removed three AI providers from its platform after discovering that they had violated their stated data-handling policies and exposed sensitive data. [...]
ffd5ce4b071046c10a21802f.title_ko: OpenRouter, 프롬프트·비밀정보 노출로 AI 제공업체 3곳 퇴출
ffd5ce4b071046c10a21802f.summary_ko: OpenRouter는 데이터 처리 정책 위반과 민감정보 노출을 확인해 Together AI·Phala·Novita를 퇴출하고, 125개 엔드포인트의 데이터 무보관 자격을 예방적으로 철회했다. Dragos는 테스트 프롬프트에 심은 인증정보가 외부 접근 시도에 사용됐다고 밝혔다. OpenRouter는 자체 시스템 침해는 없었으며, 영향을 받았을 가능성이 있는 고객에게 통지했다고 설명했다.
ffd5ce4b071046c10a21802f.background_ko: Dragos가 추적 링크와 미끼 인증정보를 넣은 테스트 프롬프트 200만 건을 전송한 뒤 외부 사용 정황을 발견하면서 제공업체의 데이터 노출 문제가 드러났다.

curation.reason_ko: 정보 노출과 처리 정책 위반으로 제공업체 3곳을 퇴출해 AI 서비스의 데이터 관리 문제가 드러났다.

7b92aff0630c3d6be364d673.title_ko: NHN KCP·KIS정보통신·웰컴페이먼츠 정보 유출…금융위, PG사 보안 점검 주문
7b92aff0630c3d6be364d673.summary_ko: NHN KCP에서는 매출전표 160건이 비정상 조회됐고, 웰컴페이먼츠에서는 1,326명의 개인신용정보가 유출됐다. KIS정보통신은 최대 862명의 개인정보가 유출됐을 가능성이 있다고 밝혔다. 금융위는 주요 PG사를 소집해 가맹점 접속 계정의 인증 절차와 노후 시스템 보안을 점검하도록 주문했다.

curation.reason_ko: 여러 PG사의 유출 사고로 금융위가 가맹점 인증과 노후 시스템 보안 점검을 요구했다.

1b256d9cbaad45021669b498.title_original: ‘rERP’ 해킹, 파장은?... 약한 고리 대학 노린 ‘산학연’ 전체 위기

curation.reason_ko: 대학들의 유출 공지와 공동연구 정보 노출 우려가 있으나 rERP 자체 결함은 확인되지 않았다.

b3df936efbe0b353b3003fb9.title_original: 미국, 메가스피드 블랙리스트 등재…황 CEO 복귀 당일 AI 칩 공급 차단

b3df936efbe0b353b3003fb9.title_ko: 미국, 메가스피드 등 7개 기업 수출통제 명단 등재…AI 칩 공급 제한
b3df936efbe0b353b3003fb9.summary_ko: 미 상무부 산업안보국이 메가스피드와 관련 계열사 등 동남아 소재 7개 기업을 수출통제 명단에 추가했다. 미국 수출관리규정 적용 대상인 반도체·소프트웨어·기술 공급에는 허가가 필요하며, 허가 신청은 원칙적으로 거부된다. 조치는 해당 규정이 적용되는 해외 생산 AI 칩에도 적용되며, 메가스피드는 중국 우회 공급 의혹을 부인해 왔다.
b3df936efbe0b353b3003fb9.background_ko: 미 상무부는 이들 기업이 첨단 컴퓨팅 제품을 허가받지 않은 최종 사용자나 용도로 전용할 위험이 상당하다고 판단했다.

curation.reason_ko: 메가스피드 등 7개 기업에 대한 수출통제로 AI 칩 공급망의 거래 조건이 바뀐다.

f802c5821b538720ab64cb8a.summary_ko: 오픈AI는 일상 대화에 맞게 조정한 GPT-6.2 솔을 챗GPT 유료 구독자에게 순차 제공한다고 밝혔다. 회사가 공개한 평가에서 이미지 이해와 복잡한 지시 수행 점수는 높아졌지만, 사용자 지시에 맞춰 응답 방식을 조정하는 능력은 하락했다. 무료 및 Go 요금제는 이번 제공 대상에서 제외된다.

02050c5de4c7b4efb904231c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31083v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI has demonstrated human-level performance on technical work tasks, yet evidence on how these task-level capabilities are changing labor demand remains scarce. We study the firm-level adoption of GitHub Copilot, an AI coding assistant, across 5,414 multinational firms accounting for 38% of the U.S. programming workforce. To identify causal effects, we exploit a natural experiment generated by firms' predetermined software procurement cycles. Early AI-adopting firms hired more workers before the launch of GitHub Copilot and had larger, more technical, and older workforces. After one year, GitHub Copilot adoption reduces quarterly technical hiring by 29% among review-induced adopters, with no effect on separations, overall technical headcount, or vacancy duration. The hiring slowdown is concentrated in the subset of junior technical roles that involve the highest share of coding work. Overall, AI coding assistance causes firms to shift demand towards more experienced workers and roles that pair some coding with broader design responsibilities.

75485d8523ee8a6c77d1d864.excerpt: On November 22nd, 2026, a threat actor pushed backdoored releases of six WordPress plugins developed by WP connect, including Air WP Sync, WP Sync for Notion, and Add-on Brevo for Gravity Forms, which together are estimated to have more than 3,600 active installations. Each release silently loaded the same remote-control module, which phones home to an attacker-controlled server, executes any PHP code it is sent, and exposes a full command set for running shell commands, stealing password hashes, and planting webshells. Thanks to safeguards introduced under WordPress.org’s Protect The Shire initiative, the backdoored versions were never released to sites, and all six plugins were closed on WordPress.org the same evening. While the WordPress plugins team independently detected and stopped this threat, Wordfence’s PRISM also discovered and notified our team to the threat, which was then validated by our team. As a reminder, PRISM is our continuous monitoring and vulnerability research agent created by the Wordfence Threat Intelligence team. The backdoor in Air WP Sync was also independently discovered and reported by Computeronfire , and we thank them for their contribution. 832b6f51cf19db4215f8d51c.title_original: ParseGap: Testing What Coding Agents Authorize and What Shells Execute
832b6f51cf19db4215f8d51c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM coding agents authorize shell commands by parsing a command string against a policy and passing the raw string to a system shell, so the gate adjudicates one reading while the shell executes another. We present ParseGap, a differential testing framework that runs each command through an unmodified vendor checker and GNU Bash 5.2 in an isolated container, flagging a violation whenever an approved command produces policy-violating runtime effects. Across eight production coding agents, ParseGap identifies 17 root causes across three divergence boundaries: at the parse, where an upstream tree-sitter-bash defect hides a second command from Mistral Vibe and Gemini CLI; at the utility, where every checker permits read-only binaries whose arguments write files or launch programs (9-47 of 55 cases); and at confinement, where an allow rule in OpenAI Codex CLI disables its read-only OS sandbox. Live trials across two frontier models triggered policy violations in all 16 agent-model pairs (14 under configured restrictions). To eliminate the second reading, we design ShellPlan, which compiles a strict Bash subset once into a typed execution plan, validates utility arguments against positive capability specifications, and dispatches approved plans directly via execve without a shell. 1f291d17a93d33734d1f6dd8.title_original: FORGETMENOT: Auditing Memory Driven Privacy Risks in Commercial AI Agents
1f291d17a93d33734d1f6dd8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Commercial AI agents increasingly incorporate long-term memory (both persistent and chat-history) to enable more accurate and personalized responses, raises significant privacy and policy concerns. Yet little is known about user privacy risks associated with memory behavior, in particular, about memory storage, disclosure, transparency and deletion control. To bridge this gap, we propose FORGETMENOT, an auditing framework for analyzing the privacy risks of long term memory in commercial AI agents. Using our framework, we collect around 3800 multi-turn sessions comprising around 6M tokens across five popular AI agents. Our results show that agents store a wide range of personal attributes, including demographics, health, and sensitive details. Furthermore, user visible memory reveals substantially less (around 20% on average) attributes than the agents store in practice, exposing a significant transparency gap. Our stealth memory injection (SMI) technique further increases the amount of personal and sensitive attribute stored in memory, raising it by 25% and 15% for Copilot and Claude, respectively. We further observed memory deletion control is unreliable, as all five agents exhibit non-zero post deletion leakage, including health and self-harm related attributes. JSON leaves some choices to each parser, such as which copy of a repeated key counts. When the guard and the executor choose differently, the guard approves one call, the executor runs another, and the audit log records the approved one. We introduce this attack, tool-call smuggling, and study it across the stack. We describe six ways in which the same bytes yield different calls and build a differential testing harness that gives identical bytes to 17 pinned parser and validator configurations; most pairs disagree on some inputs, and even two official MCP SDKs accept different inputs. On tasks from $\tau$-bench and AgentDojo, an attacker who can rewrite the bytes in transit cancels another customer's reservation and creates a file that the guard blocks by name, while the audit log names only the approved call. Content the model reads splits guard and executor only inside a string: ten models we test write no repeated or disguised key into the call itself where we see it, but copy one verbatim into JSON text in an argument, which a Python guard and a Go executor read differently. 9640affd62d136703b41bcea.title_original: CTLink: A Text-Prompted Segmentation Model for Linking Radiology Report Findings to 3D Chest CT Scans
9640affd62d136703b41bcea.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31222v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Radiology reports describe findings in text only, without visually marking them on the scan, so readers cannot directly see which abnormality each reported finding refers to. We introduce CTLink, a text-prompted 3D segmentation model that segments findings described in a chest CT report. CTLink was trained on 4123 noncontrast chest CT scans with 9547 segmented report findings, including ReXGroundingCTv2, a newly annotated dataset of 1134 scans and 1895 findings with every instance of each finding segmented. On the 200 ReXGroundingCT validation scans, CTLink achieved a hit rate of 0.816, an instance F1 score of 0.456, and a mean Dice score of 0.400, compared with 0.533, 0.175, and 0.234 for VoxTell, a publicly available text-prompted segmentation model (P < .001 for all). On the test set of the MICCAI 2026 ReXGrounding challenge, an ensemble of seven CTLink models achieved the highest hit rate (0.782) and instance F1 score (0.386) of all 48 participating teams. On 50 test scans segmented twice by independent radiologists, CTLink matched or exceeded inter-rater agreement. Diffuse non-focal findings remained the main limitation, partly because their extent is outlined inconsistently even between radiologists. The CTLink model weights are available at https://huggingface.co/rajpurkarlab/CTLink, and the dataset at https://huggingface.co/datasets/rajpurkarlab/ReXGroundingCT.

0419a40675846c3d6aaab08f.title_ko: 멤텐서·엔비디아, 대화 기억을 내부에 저장하는 멤T-1.0 프로 공개

curation.reason_ko: 대화를 내부 기억으로 활용하는 모델의 가중치·코드를 공개했으며 세부 근거 검색의 한계도 제시했다.

60fddaa0bf0d9799399ac429.title_ko: AWS, AI 에이전트 도구 작업 증가에 자체 CPU·클라우드 인프라 강화
60fddaa0bf0d9799399ac429.summary_ko: AWS는 AI 에이전트의 API 호출·코드 실행 같은 도구 작업을 지원하기 위해 자체 CPU 그래비톤 중심의 인프라를 강화한다고 밝혔다. 에이전트 작업의 80%를 CPU가 처리한다는 설명과 함께 AWS AI 팩토리와 격리 실행 환경을 소개하고, 기업 데이터를 지식 그래프로 연결하는 AWS 컨텍스트 출시 계획도 공개했다.

curation.reason_ko: AWS가 에이전트의 도구 실행을 위한 CPU 인프라와 격리 환경, 기업 데이터 연결 전략을 제시했다.

845ecd9ec2b79898433556a3.title_ko: GPT제로 5.0 출시…자체 평가서 사람 글 오판율 0.002% 주장
845ecd9ec2b79898433556a3.summary_ko: GPT제로는 AI 텍스트 탐지 모델 5.0을 공개하고, 외부 연구진이 구축한 9개 데이터셋을 활용한 자체 평가에서 최고 수준의 성능을 기록했다고 밝혔다. 사람이 작성한 300단어 이상 글 180만건 이상에서 오판율이 0.002%였다고 주장했으며, 입증된 오판 사례에는 최대 1000달러를 지급한다.

36e9bbbab7d01985273c298e.title_ko: 전남광주통합특별시, 서남권 AI 진단·전문의 원격협진망 추진

030b3a72b9b79750e9d75c8b.title_original: Don't Test Where You Trained: Geographic Overlap Inflates End-to-End Driving Scores
030b3a72b9b79750e9d75c8b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In NAVSIMv1, the standard benchmark for end-to-end driving, $89.6\%$ of the test scenes lie within 4m of a training scene. We show that this geographic overlap inflates the reported scores. We propose a geographically disjoint split of NAVSIMv1 and an evaluation that compares models trained on either split on the same scenes, which neither has seen in training. All sensor-based models we test, DiffusionDrive, Latent TransFuser, and DrivoR, lose 3.4 to 6.1 PDMS points on these scenes, mainly by leaving the road and coming close to other objects, against 1.5 points for a baseline without sensors. The loss concentrates where a training drive of the original split passed the same place. At all other places, models trained on the original split are no better than those trained on the geographic split. Models trained on the original split predict road geometry that no camera can see. The gap persists when the auxiliary map loss is removed, so the models memorize locations even without being supervised to. On nuScenes, the geographic split cuts SparseDrive's mapping accuracy by $59\%$ and also degrades its planning. Driving scores on logged scenes thus partly measure how well a model remembers the test locations. We release the split to evaluate generalization to new places.

518cbc1df8a677e18f74eea9.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28968v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hospitals often update a deployed risk model by adding a data source, such as laboratory results, that only some patients have. We compared each update with ordinary retraining on the old inputs, predicting ICU admission or death and hospital admission, on 78,475 emergency department visits from MC-MED and, in a pre-registered replication, 100,000 stays from MIMIC-IV-ED at a second hospital. Radiograph report text gave no detectable gain and almost no extra re-ranking. Laboratory results improved prediction but, at both hospitals and with linear or tree models, pushed patients without labs down alert lists; linear updates also reshuffled them more than retraining did, without ranking them better. A top-20% admission list caught 4.2% of admitted patients without labs after the update, against 18.8% after retraining (second hospital: 4.9% against 22.6%), while catching more patients overall. 8b0f56177cc27d7a3b46250b.title_original: SayDo: Benchmarking the Safety of Frontier Models from Chat to Closed-Loop Robot Control
8b0f56177cc27d7a3b46250b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30957v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Frontier vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as high-level robot controllers, yet their safety is evaluated almost entirely in text. We introduce SayDo, a benchmark that assesses the propensity of frontier models to cause harm in embodied contexts. SayDo comprises eleven laboratory and household tasks that pair a benign instruction with a hazard latent in the scene. Tasks are implemented in six settings along an embodiment gradient, from chat questions about an imagined robot to closed-loop control of a simulated robot arm. Benign controls, safe-alternative variants and scripted operator pushback complement each task. Across six open- and closed-weight VLMs and 11,480 episodes, hazardous-action rates rise from 14% in chat to 47% in the simulator, and from 2% to 80% for the most affected model. The increase is largely driven by open-weight models. We find that models flag hazards before acting in 73% of unsafe episodes and give way to pushback about twice as often when controlling robots as in chat. The safest models also show signs of overcaution on benign controls. Safety evaluations run in text therefore do not predict the safety behavior of the same models when used as robot controllers.
8b0f56177cc27d7a3b46250b.title_ko: SayDo 연구, 대화보다 로봇 제어에서 높아지는 AI 위험 행동 측정

8b0f56177cc27d7a3b46250b.background_ko: 시각언어모델이 로봇의 상위 제어기로 점점 더 활용되지만, 안전성 평가는 거의 텍스트에만 의존하고 있다.

0f7c00b0c3e14bf11f89d700.title_original: Can Vibe Coding Produce Accessible Websites: An Empirical Study on LLM Coding Agents and Skills
0f7c00b0c3e14bf11f89d700.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29822v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding agents increasingly allow developers and non-professionals to create websites through natural-language instructions, with limited inspection of the generated source code. Although this ``vibe coding'' workflow lowers barriers to software creation, it may also propagate accessibility defects at scale. We evaluated complete interaction journeys using axe-core, IBM Equal Access Accessibility Checker, and QualWeb, and converged reports to observe violation prevalence and violated WCAG Success Criterion (SC). None of the 90 baseline websites was fully accessible, with an average of 80.43 violated interface elements. 13 WCAG SCs were violated at least once across the runs. Color contrast was the most prevalent issue, followed by labeling, semantic-structure, keyboard, and visualization failures. We reran 24 matched configurations with a general accessibility Skill and a contrast-specific Skill. Both significantly improved accessibility scores, but neither eliminated violations. 0f7c00b0c3e14bf11f89d700.title_ko: 바이브 코딩 웹사이트 90개 접근성 평가…모두 결함 발견

ea1feb4b17231a8348edac9a.title_original: When Tools Fail, Agents Fabricate: Silent Failure and Verification-First Oversight in Tool-Using LLM Agents
ea1feb4b17231a8348edac9a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using LLM agents must recover when a tool call fails, by retrying, switching tools, or revising their plan. Evaluating four agents over 2,100 faulted runs against ground truth, we find that recovery is unreliable (19-68% correct) and frequently silent: 6-26% of runs end in a confident fabrication, a wrong answer asserted as fact. The failure mode is governed more by the fault type than by the model: faults that return partial data drive fabrication (up to 38%), while hard denials drive honest failure. The mechanism is what we call silent ingestion: the agent accepts faulted data as valid on first contact without retrying or flagging the problem, then builds a fabricated answer on top of it. We show that fabrication is reducible: a verification-first Monitor, grounding checks in structured tool outputs and issuing corrective directives rather than hard blocks, raises correct recovery from 45.6% to 56.3% and cuts fabrication from 17.3% to 10.8%. ea1feb4b17231a8348edac9a.title_ko: 도구 오류 뒤 답을 지어내는 LLM 에이전트…검증 우선 감독 효과 연구
ea1feb4b17231a8348edac9a.summary_ko: 연구진은 도구 오류를 주입한 2,100회 실험에서 에이전트의 올바른 복구율이 19~68%였고, 6~26%는 틀린 답을 사실처럼 제시했다고 보고했다. 특히 일부 데이터만 반환되는 오류에서 문제가 두드러졌다. 구조화된 도구 출력을 확인하는 감독 방식을 적용하자 정답 복구율은 45.6%에서 56.3%로 높아지고 허위 답변 비율은 17.3%에서 10.8%로 낮아졌다.

0947f21d19fa7609add11dd2.title_original: SchemaCaps: When a Compatible Tool Update Silently Widens an AI Agent's Authority
0947f21d19fa7609add11dd2.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The tools users approve for their AI agents keep changing their JSON input schemas. Of 8 surveyed MCP clients and scanners, none is observed or documented to re-approve a tool whose input schema widens (two not determinable). We define non-amplification over the coordinates visible in the schema (declared arguments and undeclared fields, on effective values) and a re-binding rule decided by subschema inclusion, trusting no field labels by default and conservative up to its checker and tested case analysis. Evidence: a Coq proof of composition; 48 regression tests; an exact-reference benchmark, where the reviewed version of the rule silently re-bound 27 amplifying changes, now fixed; and a pilot on 604 releases of 39 public MCP servers. There, 412 of 580 compatible schema changes widen some coordinate, yet compatibility re-binds them silently. The authors' adjudicated double annotation finds at least 76 that add or widen an authority-bearing argument (66 of the 84 a name-based labeller flags, plus 10 it misses). On existing tools, the rule asks 645 re-approvals, against 1,197 for pinning the input schema (2,004 with descriptions) and 617 for compatibility. Behaviour change behind an identical schema remains out of reach.

0947f21d19fa7609add11dd2.summary_ko: 연구진은 MCP 서버 39종의 604개 릴리스를 분석해 호환 가능한 입력 스키마 변경 580건 중 412건이 일부 입력 범위를 넓혔다고 보고했다. 연구진 판정으로 최소 76건은 권한 관련 인자를 추가하거나 확장했다. SchemaCaps는 재승인이 필요한 변경을 가려내는 규칙을 제안하지만, 스키마가 같은 상태에서 발생하는 동작 변화는 다루지 못한다.

76c62788efc9eef438d488a1.title_original: Carried-Over and Agent-Native Threats in the Supply Chain of LLM Agent Skills
76c62788efc9eef438d488a1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills are reusable packages that extend a large language model (LLM) agent with scripts, third-party dependencies, and natural-language instructions. We screen all skills by static analysis, manually review all 3,428 cases flagged by the four main detectors, and test reachability by running sampled flagged skills in a sandbox and with a live LLM agent under indirect prompt injection. First, dependency risk carries over in a different form: 49.6% of the skills with resolvable dependencies depend on a version with a known CVE, and unlike npm packages, which mostly become vulnerable after release, 78.3% of them are born vulnerable, already exposed at publication. 76c62788efc9eef438d488a1.title_ko: LLM 에이전트 스킬 공급망 분석…취약점 경고와 실제 악용 경로의 차이

5ae16873d6dc090132faf201.title_original: Who Is Prompt-Injecting Coding Agents? An Empirical Study of Hidden AI-Directed Text on GitHub
5ae16873d6dc090132faf201.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI coding agents now triage issues, review pull requests and pick up tasks inside GitHub repositories, and to do so they read text that anyone with a GitHub account can write. This makes GitHub a prime surface for indirect prompt injection, in which instructions embedded in untrusted content steer a model that later processes it. Prior work has demonstrated such attacks against agents on GitHub in controlled settings, but how often they occur in practice, who deploys them, and for what purpose remain unknown. We present the first large-scale empirical study of AI-directed hidden text on GitHub. We analyzed roughly 145 million issues, pull requests, comments and README files, detected text that GitHub does not render to a human reader but that an agent receives in full, and filtered it with a two-stage LLM classification, a template provenance check and an exhaustive manual review. We identify 2,281 validated findings in issues, pull requests and comments (16 per million items), and AI-directed hidden text in the READMEs of 107 repositories. We find a heterogeneous ecosystem of four uses: attacks on other parties' agents, defensive text that restricts agents, content override that steers what they write, and first-party orchestration, in which projects coordinate their own agents through hidden markers. 0db845a4a698b81b86435b26.title_original: Can Latent Reasoning Drive LLM Outputs Without a Trace?
0db845a4a698b81b86435b26.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLMs typically solve complex tasks with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, which is also the main tool for monitoring them for misaligned behavior. However, standard transformers can also solve tasks with complete latent reasoning (CLR), carrying out the whole task internally and outputting only the final answer. Theory bounds the depth of CLR, the number of sequential steps it can carry out, and recent work measured it to be shallow. In this work, we ask whether CLR is deep enough for a model to pursue a hidden objective that requires reasoning. Such a model would generate a CoT that appears to solve the given task, while a latent multi-step computation decides its answer based on the hidden objective. First, we show that a simple auxiliary loss allows models to solve a multi-step task latently at least 5x deeper than previously reported. Then, in two common tasks, decision-making and code generation, we train a model to pursue such a hidden objective, which decides a loan or plants a vulnerability. The model's CoT justifies the output with no trace of the hidden objective, and a strong LLM monitor does not flag it. Finally, using activation patching, we find that the latent computation is completed before the model generates its CoT, which takes no part in it. Altogether, we show that a hidden objective that requires reasoning can go unseen by a monitor that reads only the output.
0db845a4a698b81b86435b26.title_ko: 겉으로 드러난 사고 과정 뒤에 숨은 목표…LLM 잠재 추론 감시 한계 연구

4e908dbb5d4c49d9c4e04b0e.title_original: Preflight: Agentic Last-Mile Verification for AI Software Supply Chains
4e908dbb5d4c49d9c4e04b0e.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Software dependencies execute within the trust boundary of downstream applications, yet provenance, static analysis, and package-level behavioral approaches do not directly determine how a released artifact behaves for a specific program. We present Preflight, a program-scoped pre-execution verifier for Python dependencies that extracts application-referenced symbols, iteratively synthesizes and validates function-level harnesses, executes resolved artifacts in a restricted environment, records behavioral fingerprints, and compares target behavior against prior versions when suitable baselines exist. We evaluate Preflight on four real software-supply-chain incidents under five application contexts, a 100-package benign corpus, and a controlled function-level versus import-only ablation. Preflight returns malicious verdicts in four incident contexts and a clean verdict in the LiteLLM client context, where the affected proxy-server path is not exercised. All 100 evaluated benign packages receive clean verdicts, with zero observed false positives. In a controlled ablation on Ultralytics and ctx, function-level harnesses expose malicious behavior in both incidents, whereas import-only probing exposes neither. Together, these results show that conditioning behavioral verification on the downstream program can expose security-relevant dependency behavior while remaining selective on benign workloads.
4e908dbb5d4c49d9c4e04b0e.title_ko: Preflight, 프로그램 사용 맥락에 맞춰 Python 의존성의 악성 동작 검증
4e908dbb5d4c49d9c4e04b0e.summary_ko: 연구진은 Python 의존성을 응용프로그램의 사용 맥락에 맞춰 제한된 환경에서 실행하고 동작을 검증하는 Preflight를 제안했다. 공급망 사고 4건의 5개 평가 맥락 중 4개에서 악성 판정을 내렸고, 피해 경로를 사용하지 않은 LiteLLM 클라이언트와 정상 패키지 100개는 정상으로 판정했다고 보고했다.
4e908dbb5d4c49d9c4e04b0e.background_ko: 출처 증명과 정적 분석, 패키지 단위 행동 분석만으로는 특정 프로그램에서 배포된 의존성이 실제로 어떻게 동작하는지 직접 판단하기 어렵다는 한계를 보완하려는 연구다.

a70e4426b816a7ceebb913e8.title_original: ToolFence: Fine-Grained Authorization for Secure Tool-Using LLM Agents
a70e4426b816a7ceebb913e8.excerpt: arXiv:2609.37196v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Tool-using LLM agents can be redirected by attacker-controlled content into unauthorized actions. Existing tool-level guards may miss within-tool hijacking, where an attacker preserves the intended tool but changes a sensitive argument such as a recipient or destination. We present ToolFence, a provenance-aware dynamic authorization framework that combines model-based and rule-based judges to improve detection accuracy and efficiency. An LLM compiles the authenticated user request into typed, task-scoped capabilities specifying permitted tools, effects, argument sources, workflow stages, and budgets. A deterministic monitor based on Guarded Colored Petri Net (GCPN) checks each proposed call and its concrete argument values before execution. When a legitimate step requires a missing capability, an isolated LLM judge can review the action proposal and update the GCPN monitor. We evaluate ToolFence on AgentDojo, MCPTox, ASB, and AgentLAB on four different LLMs, covering environmental prompt injection, tool poisoning, memory poisoning, and long-horizon attacks. It achieves the lowest or tied-lowest attack success rate in 15 combinations. On AgentDojo with Qwen3-max, attack success falls from 21.2\% to 0\%, with a 2.0-percentage-point reduction in clean-task utility. A measured runtime subset incurs 1.63X overhead, versus 12.95X for CaMeL. Our code is released at https://github.com/PolyLiYJ/ToolFence_v2
a70e4426b816a7ceebb913e8.title_ko: ToolFence, LLM 에이전트의 도구 호출 인자까지 검사하는 권한 관리 제안
a70e4426b816a7ceebb913e8.summary_ko: 연구진은 사용자 요청을 작업별 권한으로 변환하고 실행 전 도구 호출과 실제 인자 값을 검사하는 ToolFence를 제안했다. 4개 LLM을 이용한 평가에서 15개 조합의 공격 성공률이 최저 또는 공동 최저였으며, AgentDojo의 Qwen3-max 실험에서는 정상 작업 효용이 2%포인트 낮아지는 대신 공격 성공률이 21.2%에서 0%로 줄었다고 보고했다.

01c3627fa1db92d5a6bcfdbd.title_original: Airlock: Robust Sandboxing and Governance of Rogue Agents

a788ab219904a0b852a0b091.title_original: Zero-Trust Formal Methods: AI Agents Build Verified Checkers for Untrusted Solvers
a788ab219904a0b852a0b091.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28704v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI coding agents now generate code faster than humans can review it. Security analyses rely on solver answers such as "unsatisfiable" (for example, no attack path exists) or "optimal." Unlike satisfying models, they cannot be checked by looking at them. Formal verification moves trust from code to specifications, but verifiers still place large SAT, SMT, and answer-set solvers, and the translation into solver queries, in their trusted computing base, and these have had soundness bugs. Unlike agent-based pipelines that trust their verifier and solver, our farm trusts no component by default: neither the AI agents, which might make mistakes or game their objectives, nor the solvers. A solver answer counts only if a verified checker accepts its certificate. Every theory, proof, and line of code is generated by AI. For each component, agents first create an Isabelle/HOL theory with a specification, a soundness proof, and a reference checker made by code generation, then a fast Rust implementation, verified with Verus against a specification that mirrors the Isabelle definitions line by line. Specifications are frozen after independent review and cannot be changed by the implementing agents. A trust manifest lists what is still trusted. a788ab219904a0b852a0b091.title_ko: AI 에이전트로 솔버 답변 검사기를 만드는 ‘제로 트러스트’ 형식 검증 연구

9ae95873d5abd5160f102402.title_original: Safety Systems Watch What the Model Says, Not What the Child Says

b1c2b3d28ab605e57d890b25.title_original: Ultrasound Watermark: Real-time Acoustic Watermarking against Voice Scams on Smartphones

Existing defenses often rely on offline analysis, degrade under telephony distortions, or remain vulnerable to adaptive attacks. Ultrasound Watermark operates continuously with less than 200 ms latency overhead and requires no additional hardware. b1c2b3d28ab605e57d890b25.title_ko: 초음파로 발화 움직임 확인…통화 사칭 방어 워터마킹 연구

021603bf0109f5ece8f489cb.title_original: Social sycophancy differs across access modes of large language models
021603bf0109f5ece8f489cb.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28012v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can display sycophancy, a tendency to excessively praise, agree with, or validate a user. Existing studies have tested LLMs for sycophancy primarily through application programming interfaces (APIs) rather than the consumer user interfaces (UIs) through which the public commonly interacts with LLMs. Access mode (API vs. UI) may affect observed sycophancy rates. However, it remains unknown to what extent prominent models show API-UI differences in social sycophancy, which includes behaviors potentially more likely in UIs (e.g., softening warranted criticism). We tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek through both APIs and UIs on four dimensions of social sycophancy. Across models, UI access was generally associated with greater social sycophancy, with odds ratios up to 7.56 (95% CI [6.22, 9.20]). However, UI-API differences varied significantly across models for all sycophancy dimensions, including a pronounced reversal for DeepSeek moral sycophancy (43% UI vs. 82.3% API). Overall, our results suggest that API-based LLM evaluations may underestimate the prevalence of sycophancy in corresponding consumer-facing systems, making access conditions consequential for the external validity of LLM evaluation. To facilitate research on access-mode effects, we release 57,000 model responses and SycoUI, a browser-automation pipeline for standardized cross-interface LLM evaluation.

cd640b5aa8c8f38b28ca226d.title_original: NRSnooper: Enabling Real-Time Bidirectional Traffic Decoding in Commercial 5G NR Networks
cd640b5aa8c8f38b28ca226d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decoding both uplink and downlink cellular traffic reveals lower-layer protocol behavior, unprotected signaling, and encrypted higher-layer packets beyond what scheduling metadata exposes. In commercial 5G NR networks, however, passive decoding must overcome UE-dedicated configurations hidden in encrypted signaling, unknown identifiers of ongoing connections, and the computational demands of wideband traffic. We present NRSnooper, a passive sniffer that decodes downlink control and bidirectional data traffic in real time, including traffic from already-connected UEs and traffic after encrypted configuration updates. NRSnooper learns reusable physical-layer configurations through an instrumented open-source UE that reproduces commercial UE capabilities. It recovers connection-specific identifiers from ongoing transmissions and selects matching configurations through CRC-validated data decoding. A hybrid CPU-GPU pipeline sustains continuous wideband processing. Evaluations on a controlled testbed and two commercial networks show that, compared with using only configurations from unencrypted signaling, NRSnooper decodes 1.3x and 6.3x as many control messages and 9.0x and 17.7x as many downlink data blocks, respectively. NRSnooper also decodes traffic from an already-connected UE during an ongoing phone call and achieves real-time bidirectional decoding on 100 MHz commercial NR channels.

b71ed2858cece97d5dca9f99.title_original: Into My Arms: Structured reinforcement learning for autonomous transport of objects and humans
b71ed2858cece97d5dca9f99.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Whole-body humanoid manipulation remains bottlenecked by high-dimensional state-action spaces, contact-rich environments, and long task horizons. This trilemma is a challenge that state-of-the-art reinforcement learning (RL) methods are yet to resolve reliably. We address it with three contributions that add just enough structure to guide exploration: Sparse Interaction Edges (SIE) for whole-body manipulation, Interaction Gated Transport (IGT) for sustained transport over long horizons, and a Hinted Object Path (HOP) that resolves collision and search complexity bottlenecks. Across all three, the policy remains free to discover its own manipulation strategy. The method generalises from rigid object to human transport. As a flagship demonstration, we show, to our knowledge, the first bed-to-wheelchair transfer of a medical mannequin by a humanoid robot completed with no human intervention during execution. In the domain of human transfer, we show that a single policy can adapt across substantial variations in body mass, size, and random force perturbations, all while training on a single GPU in under an hour. Our approach offers a pathway to fully RL-driven humanoid manipulation, enabling assistive robots that can help humans. Website: https://elle-miller.github.io/into_my_arms

0edf1d4b0a7ff907b192c75c.title_original: What Makes Good Data for Training Coding Agents? A Systematic Study on SWE-Gym
0edf1d4b0a7ff907b192c75c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30207v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) trains coding agents on software tasks whose hidden tests decide the reward, yet task collections check these tests only against the reference fix. We ask what makes a task good training data, focusing on the correctness of its reward labels. We audit SWE-Gym with two LLM families, and a suspected error counts only if execution reproduces it. We find that unsolved often means mislabelled: 74% of the tasks that a 9B base model never solves have a test that rejects correct fixes (a false negative), versus 20% of those it sometimes solves. We repair or remove such tasks, and the audited tasks that remain train better policies. At equal size and matched difficulty, models trained on them score 2.4 and 2.7 points higher on held-out tasks from SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Pro than models trained on the original tasks, whereas simply dropping the never-solved tasks shows no such gain. We further find that wrong patches that pass (false positives) make up about a quarter of all passing patches, and that new tests that catch a quarter of them do not change held-out scores detectably. A pass rate shows whether a task yields reward, not whether that reward is right, so the reward labels themselves must be checked. To this end, we release SWE-Gym-Verified with its 1,087 audited tasks, every verdict with its executed evidence, our training sets, and the full audit pipeline.

f8c5529210ec448b6ab2a430.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stateful LLM serving engines and agent runtimes reuse execution state and deferred permissions across components and sessions. A cancellation, rollback, or approval is recorded by one component and relied on by another, and recording it does not make the later use valid: a downstream consumer may read state or dispatch an action whose identity, production status, allocation, or target revision has since changed. We call the missing check consumer-time validity and separate two forms. State validity governs what a consumer reads. On vLLM with LMCache, an interrupted KV load leaves unwritten blocks indexed, and a host-only counter rewind desynchronizes the GPU position, so a second tenant generates a schema-valid tool call naming the wrong tenant in 10/10 native-fault runs; the call is recorded and not executed. Authority freshness governs what a consumer executes: on a multi-session approval runtime, an unrevoked deferred grant overwrote a newer revision in one admitted live execution. Output equality cannot test state validity: a fault-free run diverges at token 30 through BF16 batching alone while attended-KV digests match. We therefore specify consumer-bound recovery contracts that, for state recovery, jointly require exclusion, retention, and task completion, and an admissible-witness standard realized as a GPU-free offline trace verifier over scheduler metadata and persisted tool artifacts. Security researchers are using AI coding agents to find vulnerabilities faster. So are attackers. Now researchers increasingly do that work with AI coding tools and agentic security testing harnesses. In April, we reported that AI-assisted reports had grown from 16% to roughly 66% of submissions to our Bug Bounty Program . e7202f0c37a0f8ad5c1d8290.excerpt: arXiv:2601.20245v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: AI assistance produces significant productivity gains across professional domains, particularly for novice workers. Yet how this assistance affects the development of skills required to effectively supervise AI remains unclear. Novice workers who rely heavily on AI to complete unfamiliar tasks may compromise their own skill acquisition in the process. We conduct randomized experiments to study how developers gained mastery of a new asynchronous programming library with and without the assistance of AI. We find that AI use impairs conceptual understanding, code reading, and debugging abilities, without delivering significant efficiency gains on average. Participants who fully delegated coding tasks showed some productivity improvements, but at the cost of learning the library. We identify six distinct AI interaction patterns, three of which involve cognitive engagement and preserve learning outcomes even when participants receive AI assistance. Our findings suggest that AI-enhanced productivity is not a shortcut to competence and AI assistance should be carefully adopted into workflows to preserve skill formation -- particularly in safety-critical domains.

c11e0960a516aedac8b803e1.title_original: TurboFHE: An Efficient and Scalable Multi-GPU Framework for Homomorphic LLM Inference
c11e0960a516aedac8b803e1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving large language model inference but remains computationally intensive. Existing multi-GPU FHE inference systems rely on expert-crafted parallelization plans that generalize poorly across hardware platforms and applications. We present \fwName, a framework that automatically compiles CKKS inference programs into efficient multi-GPU executables. Its compiler can split different nodes of the same computation graph at the ciphertext and polynomial level. Guided by a measurement-based performance model, its hardware-aware planner jointly optimizes task partitioning, placement, operand residency, and transfer scheduling. %Critical-path-guided rewrites extract shared computation and restructure homomorphic sums. Its backend then generates optimized GPU kernels and executes plans using CUDA graphs and selective point-to-point transfers. \fwName adapts its plans to diverse hardware configurations and FHE inference algorithms for large-scale models. On a single A100 GPU, \fwName achieves a $24.5\times$ speedup over THOR's reported BERT-Base inference latency. For Cerium's Llama-3-8B workload, \fwName outperforms Cerium's expert-crafted plans by $1.14\times$, $1.16\times$, and $1.24\times$ on 2, 4, and 8 RTX PRO~6000 GPUs, respectively. On A100 GPUs, \fwName achieves $98.0\%$, $91.8\%$, and $79.3\%$ parallel efficiency for the same workload on 2, 4, and 8 GPUs, respectively.

b8248adaa94b0a9f4ee2bace.title_original: Grower-in-the-loop AI for Deployable Precision Fertilisation in Sustainable Agriculture
b8248adaa94b0a9f4ee2bace.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In agriculture, typically over half of the applied nitrogen fertiliser is lost to water and to air. Precision fertilisation aims to reduce these losses while maintaining yield and quality, yet existing tools struggle to capture farm-specific challenges in determining optimal nitrogen rates. Static recommendations are common and overlook on-farm constraints, such as delays due to weather or machinery availability, or change in budgets. Here we present a grower-in-the-loop framework for winter wheat in England, combining baseline fertilisation planning from a machine learning-derived nitrogen-response curve with in-season adaptation via a large language model. We evaluated the framework using data from long-term experiments (LTEs), replicated field trials, and farm deployments. Retrospective model validation using LTEs confirmed low economic decision-loss across multiple seasons. Using field and farm trials, baseline schedules were shown to match standard-practice yields with less nitrogen, whereas in-season adjusted schedules additionally retained grain quality standards.
